div.head: In Cn II 15.1b
div.ab: In lege eorum liberalis hominis lahslit uocant X dimidię marcę, hoc est V marcę; hominis alodium (bocland) habentis sex dimidię marcę, hoc est tres marcę; uillani lahslit, quem Angli uocant ceorlman XII orę.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 612 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: nämlich Danorum. Diese Busssätze zahlen bezw. cyninges þegn [liberalis setzen Inst. oft für þegn], landagende, cyrlisc man nach Northu. 51 ff., o. S. 383, deren Benutzung hierfür auch Steenstrup Danelag 267 annimmt

namely Danorum. These rates of compensation are paid respectively by the cyninges þegn [the Inst. often put liberalis for þegn], the landagende and the cyrlisc man according to Northu. 51 ff., above p. 383, which Steenstrup Danelag 267 also assumes to have been used here
in the 12th cent. 1 mark = ⅔ pound
only H, written above, missing in the rest
Vgl. Gl Rechtsbruchbusse 5. 8a; Thegn 22; gemeinfrei 9b; Ör 4b; Halbmark 3; Allod 1
Cf. Gl Rechtsbruchbusse 5. 8a; Thegn 22; gemeinfrei 9b; Ör 4b; Halbmark 3; Allod 1

div.ab: In their law they call the lahslit [fine for breach of law] of a free man of rank (thegn) ten half-marks, that is five marks; of a man having allodial land (bocland) six half-marks, that is three marks; the lahslit of a villein, whom the English call ceorlman, twelve ores.
